sections.h2: Where is Cicero, NY, and what is the town like?
sections.html:
Cicero is a lakeside suburb of Syracuse in the northeastern part of Onondaga County. Oneida Lake lies along its northern edge, the Oneida River marks the border with Oswego County, and Chittenango Creek marks the line with Madison County. The town covers about 48.5 square miles, and a large swamp, Cicero Swamp, sits in its southeastern part.

The town began in 1790 as a township in the Central New York Military Tract, separated from Lysander in 1807, and lost its western half in 1827 when that portion became the town of Clay. Interstate 81, U.S. Route 11 and Routes 31 and 298 pass through, and the reconstructed Erie Canal follows the Oneida River along the north line. A small corner of Syracuse Hancock International Airport reaches the southern town line, and Michael Airfield, a single-runway general aviation field, is inside the town.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and school districts shape a Cicero sale?
sections.html:
Much of the town is wetland, forest and farm land, with a growing number of housing developments pushing onto the farmland. Hamlets include Brewerton near the northern line, Bridgeport (partly in Madison County), Cicero Center on Route 31, and shoreline settlements such as Kraus Landing, Forest Beach and Lower South Bay. The Village of North Syracuse lies partly inside the town on its western edge.

Four school districts bill taxes on Cicero parcels. The town's tax receiver processes school taxes for North Syracuse Central Schools, and for the Chittenango, Central Square and East Syracuse-Minoa districts on properties in the town. Buyers will ask which district serves an address, so confirm it from the school line on the tax bill.

  • Subdivisions named in local descriptions include Bay Colony near South Bay, The Crossings, and Lyon's Runne near Oneida Lake.
  • Lakeshore settlements such as Kraus Landing and Valentine's Beach sit on Oneida Lake north of Cicero Center.
  • Interstate 81 and U.S. 11 meet near the hamlet of Cicero in the southwest.

sections.h2: How is a Cicero house assessed, and when is the next Grievance Day?
sections.html:
The Assessor's office values every parcel in Cicero, handles veteran, senior and disability exemptions, and tracks sales data and the equalization rate. The tentative roll was published May 1, 2026, and the town reports a 53 percent level of assessment, an equalization rate of 53 percent and a residential assessment ratio of 53 percent. A house assessed at $150,000 would therefore be viewed as having a market value of roughly $283,000 under that ratio.

The 2026 Grievance Day has already passed. The town posts the next Board of Assessment Review date as Tuesday, May 25, 2027, with hearings by appointment only at the Cicero Town Meeting Room, 8236 Brewerton Road, from 12 to 2 p.m. and 6 to 8 p.m. Complaints must be filed by 3:00 p.m. that day on form RP-524, and the town accepts them in the Town Hall drop box, by mail or by email.

  • Taxable status date is March 1, and the town page says completed exemption applications may be submitted through March 1, 2027.
  • From 2026 the State decides who qualifies for the Basic and Enhanced STAR exemptions, so questions about STAR go to the State, not the Assessor.
  • Informal reviews with the Assessor happen before Grievance Day, and the final roll is dated July 1.

sections.h2: When are Cicero property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Cicero's Receiver of Taxes processes the town and county bill, the North Syracuse village bill and the school bills. The town and county bill is mailed around January 1 and is due without penalty on February 2. School bills are mailed around September 1 and are due without penalty around October 1. Village bills (for the part of North Syracuse in town) are mailed around June 1 and due July 1.

Partial payments are accepted if nothing delinquent is owed, and the first payment must reach the office by the no-penalty date. Town and county bills can be split into up to four payments, village bills into three, and school bills into three. Mail counts as paid on its postmark date, but a postage meter mark does not count.

The tax office has one caution for sellers. It takes two to three months after a deed is filed with the county for the Assessor's records to reflect the new owner, so call the tax office when you buy or sell. Until the records change, the bill goes to the owner on file.

sections.h2: What do Cicero zoning and code rules mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The Department of Zoning and Planning issues building permits and enforces the town code from the Town Hall on Brewerton Road. A Certificate of Occupancy is issued once all work under a permit is complete and outside inspection certificates for plumbing and electrical have been received. Anything built without a permit cannot receive a Certificate of Occupancy or a Certificate of Compliance, and the town may issue a stop work order and fines.

Residents are told to find their zoning on the tax bill or the town zoning map. The office lists these permit triggers.

  • Permits are needed to add on, demolish, change occupancy, move doors and windows, repair fire damage or install a fence.
  • Fireplaces, woodstoves and heat-producing devices also need permits.
  • Ordinary repairs, siding, roofing over no more than two layers, and windows or doors of equal size need no permit.
  • A permit lasts 12 months from issue.

Plan review for a new dwelling can run two to six weeks, so an unpermitted addition is better settled before you list.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded for a Cicero house in Onondaga County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Cicero parcels are recorded by the Onondaga County Clerk, and county records reach back to 1794. The base fee for a deed is $45.50 plus $5 per page, and transfer tax is $4 per thousand dollars of price. A TP-584 return costs $5, the RP-5217 form costs $125 for improved residential or agricultural property and $250 for improved commercial property or vacant land, and a $10 charge applies to residential deeds.

State law puts the base transfer tax on the seller, at $2 for every $500 of price, and the TP-584 is due within 15 days of the deed. Recording is also where a mansion tax of 1 percent attaches to residences at $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it. The clerk's office closes every first Tuesday of the month from 10:30 to 11:00 a.m. for a staff meeting, which is a small thing worth knowing if you are timing a closing run.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cicero, New York?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 31,435 residents, down 0.8 percent from the 31,682 counted in 2010.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day for Cicero property owners?
faqs.a: The Cicero assessor posts Tuesday, May 25, 2027 as the next Board of Assessment Review date. Complaints must be in by 3:00 p.m. that day, and hearings are by appointment.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Cicero property taxes to?
faqs.a: Pay the Cicero Receiver of Taxes at Town Hall, 8236 Brewerton Road, Cicero, NY 13039. The office collects town, county, village and school taxes for parcels in town.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cicero house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: You can sell it, but the town cannot issue a Certificate of Occupancy or Compliance for work done without a permit. Call Zoning and Planning to learn what the town would require.

faqs.q: What does the county charge to record a deed in Onondaga County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $45.50 plus $5 per page, with $5 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217 on residential property. Transfer tax is $4 per thousand dollars of price.
